summary: Frontend-only verification of Ask-AI send button fix in the static app at /app/index.html. Verified sendMsg() fires on desktop click, Enter key, quick-chip regression, mobile touchend on #sendBtn, click on inner SVG (bubbling), and Shift+Enter inserts a newline without sending. Disabled-guard correctly prevents double-send while an AI request is in-flight.
critical_code_review_comments: wireChatSend IIFE runs at parse time; because 05-exam-prep.js is loaded after the DOM defines #sendBtn/#msgInput, this works — but a defensive DOMContentLoaded wrap would be safer for future refactors.

The click and touchend handlers are both bound; on real touch devices, a tap fires touchend AND then a synthetic click. The disabled-guard prevents the double-send race, but adding e.stopPropagation() or a small timestamp de-dupe would be even cleaner.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix verified. Test approach: navigate via page.evaluate("goTo('pg-app'); goPanel('chat');") to bypass auth. Use synthetic TouchEvent dispatch for mobile-tap simulation (Playwright default context has no touch support). Note the disabled-guard means back-to-back tests must wait for prior AI reply (or reset sb.disabled) before firing next tap.
verified_behaviors: Desktop click on #sendBtn -> user bubble added, input cleared
Enter key on #msgInput -> user bubble added, input cleared
Quick-chip .qchip click -> user bubble added (regression pass)
Mobile touchend on #sendBtn (dispatched TouchEvent) -> user bubble added, input cleared
Click on inner <svg> inside #sendBtn -> user bubble added (event bubbles to parent handler)
Touchend on inner SVG -> listener fires (preventDefault confirmed via dispatchEvent()==false); disabled-guard correctly blocks double-send
